<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**18** anchor(s) derived from **3** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **46** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 05563a57f00f60223ccb4974db444c8231f1fd9d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4683161efc6b538a75ecd2fb48e9426d2615ce88` — the merge of head `d6092ff79df63ec50fcaa457ca84d2787029f838` into base `05563a57f00f60223ccb4974db444c8231f1fd9d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4683161efc6b538a75ecd2fb48e9426d2615ce88 && git checkout 4683161efc6b538a75ecd2fb48e9426d2615ce88
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 05563a57f00f60223ccb4974db444c8231f1fd9d d6092ff79df63ec50fcaa457ca84d2787029f838 && git checkout -B drift-repro 05563a57f00f60223ccb4974db444c8231f1fd9d && git merge --no-ff d6092ff79df63ec50fcaa457ca84d2787029f838

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 05563a57f00f60223ccb4974db444c8231f1fd9d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `d12137d7ca7f0505e2b766db7dfd7563b80b4ddd`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #37598 (body, triage, claim, os-dev-report), PR #37652 (body, 8 files), `git diff origin/main...pr-37652-a`, and the 68 check-runs on the head (57 success, 11 skipped, 0 failure: TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates, Check Changeset, Test Core 10/10 and aggregate, Dogfood Regression Gate among them).

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set: no change. Nothing under `packages/spec/**`, no schema, no authorable key, no response body. Right.

Public surface, each change the diff publishes:
- `@objectstack/types` (published, `publishConfig`; root entry is `export * from './server-fault-log.js'`): three NEW exports, `faultCauseChain`, `FAULT_CAUSE_DEPTH_LIMIT` and `FaultCauseLine`. This is additive, and it is mis-declared (M1). The core parity test imports `faultCauseChain` from the package root, so the export is load-bearing and cannot simply be made private.
- `@objectstack/types` `logServerFault`: the console fallback line gains `causes` beside `stack`. The injected-logger branch is unchanged: it still hands `toError(input.error)`, the same object with `cause` intact. This is additive for log consumers. Right.
- `@objectstack/core` `ObjectLogger`: an error record goes from `{ message, stack }` to `{ message, stack, causes? }`. `renderError`, `causeOf` and `causeLine` are module-private. The change is additive, and `causes` is absent when there is no cause. Right in shape, but see S1 and S2.
- `@objectstack/service-record-context`: `describeThrown` was module-private, so no export is removed. `failure.stack` no longer carries the `Caused by:` suffix that #37550 added. That changes the log text, not the wire, and is acceptable only because both in-repo sinks now render `cause` (see S3 for the sinks outside the repo).

Wire: no path puts `faultCauseChain` or `error.causes` on an answer. `faultCauseChain` is called from the `logServerFault` console branch only. `renderError` is called from `ObjectLogger.write` only. Neither `response-envelope.ts` nor `serverFaultLogMeta` carries a stack or a cause. Both the harness (both MCP doors: no `causes` and no `Caused by` in the answer text) and the `sendServerFault` case (generic envelope) pin this. Right.

Findings:
- M1 (must-fix) — `Clause-②: no` is wrong. The diff adds three exports to the published `@objectstack/types` root. Under seat precedent a new export on a published package is `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, still at patch. Fix the line in BOTH the PR body and `.changeset/37598-fault-log-cause-chain.md`, and keep all three packages at `patch`. The card prescribed `no`, but the card wrote its prescription before the export existed, and the diff decides.
- S1 (should-fix) — security-relevant, in the `ObjectLogger` non-Error cause path (`causeLine` in `packages/core/src/logger.ts`). The details go to the seat out of band and are not repeated here.
- S2 (should-fix) — only a throwing `cause` getter is guarded. A cause whose `name`, `message` or `stack` read throws (a hostile getter, or a Proxy) costs the whole record. In `logServerFault` the outer `catch` returns `false` and the fault line is never written; before this diff the same input logged. In `ObjectLogger.write`, `renderError` sits outside any `try`, so `logger.error` throws to its caller. The fix is to wrap `causeLine` per link and emit a marker link on a throw, in both copies, and to add the case to the parity fixtures.
- N1 (nit) — both docblocks say "`logger.test.ts` pins the two to one output", but the parity block is in `packages/core/src/logger-error-cause.test.ts`.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/types`, `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/service-record-context` matches what the diff publishes: a bug fix plus additive exports and additive log fields. Nothing is removed or narrowed, so no BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 marker is owed. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing a metadata author can write changes.

Clause-②: wrong as declared. It should read `yes (widening)`, because of the three new `@objectstack/types` exports (M1). The new log output shape (`causes` on the console fallback, `error.causes` on `ObjectLogger`) is an additive widening for log consumers: no existing field changes meaning or goes missing.

### ③ Boundary flags

Security-touching: yes

`open_questions`: none in the report. `security_findings: none` in the report: disagreed, see S1.

Dev flag (out-of-scope finding, "noted, not filed"): `@objectstack/observability` `ConsoleLogger` and `JsonLogger` record an error as `{ error, stack }` without `cause`. The flag is real. No in-repo door is handed one (the MCP doors use the console fallback, and the dispatcher uses the kernel logger). Both are public exports a host can inject, though. For such a host, removing the record-context `Caused by:` suffix turns a logged root cause back into a lost one.
- S3 (should-fix) — file the follow-up card for the observability loggers instead of `carrier: none`. This is not blocking for this head.

Seat questions:
1. Wire: never. The chain feeds only the console fallback meta and the `ObjectLogger` record. No answer builder reads either, and the harness on both doors plus the `sendServerFault` case pin the answer bodies. Operator-only holds.
2. Disclosure: yes, it is wider for log readers, in two ways. (a) An Error cause's `name: message` and stack are now printed wherever a wrapper used to hide them. Those are driver and host messages of the same class the unwrapped error already printed, so this is the card's intent, and the record-context path already printed them through the suffix. (b) The non-Error cause path in `ObjectLogger` is a new concern (S1). The console fallback was never redacted, so it has no new mechanism, only new content.
3. Parity: real for the branches it feeds. Five fixtures (nested Error, cycle, nine-deep chain past the limit, string cause, object cause) go through the actual JSON record and are compared with `toEqual` against `faultCauseChain`. A drift in a marker text, the depth limit, cycle handling, or Error, string or object rendering fails it. It does not cover the throwing-getter branch or a JSON-throwing or JSON-undefined object cause. The two implementations agree there by reading (`safeStringify` is identical to core's inline form), but no fixture would catch a drift. Add those cases with S2.
4. #37550 harness: yes. The real-kernel outage case asserts, on all four fault lines across both doors, that `causes[0].message` is `Error: OUTAGE` and that `causes[0].stack` contains it, and that the stack carries no `Caused by:`. The report's ablation (the `causes` spread disabled) reds this case. It proves the console-fallback sink that the MCP doors use. The `ObjectLogger` sink is proven by the core unit test, not by the harness. That is sufficient because the injected-logger branch passes the original error object unchanged.
5. Clause-②: `faultCauseChain` (with `FAULT_CAUSE_DEPTH_LIMIT` and `FaultCauseLine`) is a new export of the published `@objectstack/types`, so the line must be `Clause-②: yes (widening)` at patch (M1). The log shape change is an additive widening for log consumers and does not change the level.

SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): the diff has no data access, no id materialisation and no in-app join. No finding.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `5a623151013b8fc71ea913cdbec0a727be96cdd7`
Local-runs: none

Delta review: prior head `d12137d7ca7f0505e2b766db7dfd7563b80b4ddd`, now `5a623151013b8fc71ea913cdbec0a727be96cdd7` (2 commits). Read: the delta diff (5 files, +152 / -15), the net diff against main (the same 8 files, +583 / -24), the PR body, the seat REWORK 7200035097, the dev delta report 7200784938, card #37658, and the 72 check-runs on the head (59 success, 13 skipped, 0 failure, all completed).

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set: unchanged and empty. There is no spec, schema or response-body change. Public surface: the same three new `@objectstack/types` exports as before. `faultCauseChain`'s second parameter changes from a depth `limit` to a per-key redaction predicate. The export is new in this PR and has no released consumer, so the change costs nothing, and `FAULT_CAUSE_DEPTH_LIMIT` still fixes the depth. The `ObjectLogger` record shape is unchanged: `error.causes` stays optional and additive.

Prior ids:
- M1: closed. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is now in the PR body and in `.changeset/37598-fault-log-cause-chain.md`, and every package stays at `patch`.
- S1: closed. Both copies now serialize a non-Error object cause through a `JSON.stringify` replacer. `ObjectLogger` passes its own configured redact rule (`isRedactedFieldName`), so the cause follows the same rule as the record's fields. The replacer runs at every depth, so nested objects and objects inside arrays are covered too (the `types` test pins `nested.authToken`). Value-borne text is not covered: a message string, or a value that `toJSON` turns into a string. That is outside the logger's existing contract, which redacts by field name only and has never scrubbed an error's own `message`. Not a finding.
- S2: closed. Each link is read inside a guard in both copies. A throwing `name`, `message` or `stack` read ends the chain in `[cause chain link unreadable: reading it threw]`, and the record is still written: `logServerFault` returns `true`, and `ObjectLogger` no longer throws. The `String(cause)` fallback is inside the same guard. The parity fixtures cover the case.
- S3: closed. #37658 (open) carries the observability loggers, and the PR body names it.
- N1: closed. Both docblocks name `logger-error-cause.test.ts`.

New:
- S4 (should-fix): the console fallback's default rule is a substring match (`lower.includes(word)`), while `ObjectLogger`'s rule matches on word boundaries.
  - Because of that, the fallback redacts the values under bare `keys` and `tokens`, and under `monkey`, `keyword` and `secretary`. The maintainer's ruling on #5573 says those must not be redacted. A reader sees `***REDACTED***` where nothing secret was withheld.
  - It is a superset of `ObjectLogger`'s default rule, so it leaks nothing. But the docblock says "the same rule a logger applies to its own fields", which is not what it does.
  - No parity fixture uses such a key, so the drift between the two copies is not caught.
  - Fix: align the fallback with the word-boundary rule, or narrow the docblock and add a fixture that pins the documented difference.
- N2 (nit): the `faultCauseChain` docblock says the fallback "errs towards withholding". That is true only against the default list. The fallback cannot apply a list a host configured on its logger, and the MCP doors always log through the fallback. State that limitation in the docblock.
- N3 (nit): no test pins an array inside an object cause. JSON semantics cover it, but a fixture should hold it in both copies.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/types`, `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/service-record-context` is right. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is now right: three new exports on a published package, and additive log fields. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.

### ③ Boundary flags

Security-touching: yes

`open_questions`: none. The dev's `out_of_scope_findings` entry is carried by #37658. The report gives `security_findings` as withheld; the redaction gap S1 described is closed by this head.

Host-configured words on the console fallback: a host's stricter list (for example, extra domain words) is not applied to object causes on the fallback line, which is the MCP doors' only sink. I accept this at this scope for four reasons:
- The fallback has never applied host redaction to anything (message, meta, stack). It has no logger config to read.
- The default words still apply, and more broadly than `ObjectLogger` applies them.
- No in-repo producer puts a plain object on `Error.cause`.
- The real fix is to hand the MCP doors the kernel logger, which is outside this card's surface.
Documenting the limitation is N2. A carrier card is optional.

Pre-existing, ungraded: when the top-level thrown value is a non-Error object, `toError` still stringifies it into the message without redaction. That is unchanged from `main` and not touched by this PR.

SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): there is no data access in the diff. No finding.
